# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. ```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #983._

> ℹ️ **2 resolved thread(s) excluded; 10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). ```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #983._

> ℹ️ **2 resolved thread(s) excluded; 10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;

    return false;

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 983 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/983 - **Title**: gh-960 PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952) - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-960` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 65 - **Additions**: +336 - **Deletions**: -715 - **Created**: 2026-10-17T16:46:01Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-17T22:28:44Z ## PR Description Closes #960 ### What changed The rework-publish body refresh (`postTestReworkBodyAndComment` in `js/postTestReworkResults.js`) no longer rewrites the PR body once the PR has entered the merge queue, and a pre-queue refresh now re-applies the canonical `Closes #N` line so it can never be dropped. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RW[Test rework publish] --> FROZEN{prBodyFrozen?
ai_validating / merged / closed} FROZEN -->|yes| SKIP[Skip body rewrite — body is final
gh-960] FROZEN -->|no| REFRESH[Rebuild body + ensureClosesLine
Closes #N preserved] SKIP --> CMT[Post summary comment] REFRESH --> CMT ```

Added `isPrBodyFrozen()` to `js/common/pullRequest.js`. ### Key decisions - **Freeze signal**: body is final when the PR carries `ai_validating` (validate→merge pipeline armed), or is `merged`/`closed` — the exact point after which GitHub stops parsing closing keywords (live #956/#952). - **Comment unaffected**: the rework summary comment still posts on frozen PRs; only the body rewrite is skipped. - **Closes preservation**: the refreshed body is passed through the existing `ensureClosesLine` (gh-737), so pre-queue refreshes keep the keyword the merge bot links by; non-`gh-N` keys stay untouched. ### How to verify ```bash node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_pullRequestHelper.js js/unit-tests/test_postTestReworkResults.js ```

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `isPrBodyFrozen` exceeds the CRAP threshold — CI `crap` gate fails deterministically**

The Quality workflow fails on this PR with:

```
NEW > 8  js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold ...
```

I reproduced the measurement locally with the pinned tool (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: `isPrBodyFrozen` has **CC = 12**, so even at **100% coverage** its CRAP score is 12 — above the threshold of 8. No amount of additional testing can bring this under the gate; the function itself must be simplified.

The complexity concentrates in the label scan (the `for` loop, the `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? … : …` ternary, and the `indexOf` check). Extract it into a small helper, e.g.:

```javascript
function mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels) {
    labels = labels || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        var name = labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? labels[i].name : labels[i];
        if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
    if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
    if (pr.merged === true) return true;
    var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
    return state === 'closed' || state === 'merged' || mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(pr.labels);
}
```

Both functions land well under CC 8 (helper ≈ 5, predicate ≈ 7), so the ratchet passes at full coverage. The existing unit tests pin the behavior — they should keep passing unchanged after the extraction.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the freeze guards a path that cannot be the incident's write path — the real writer is unguarded**

Two independent facts make this guard ineffective for the live incident (#956/#952):

1. **Wrong PR population.** `postTestReworkResults.js` only ever touches *test* PRs — `findTestPRForTicket` hard-filters `pr.head.ref === 'test/' + ticketKey`. The incident PR #956 (verified via `gh pr view 956`: `headRefName: ai/gh-952`, body first line `Closes #952`, `mergedAt == body updatedAt`) is a **dev PR**. This module's publish step never runs against PRs like #956.

2. **Dead seam.** The rewrite being frozen lives in `updatePullRequestBody` behind `scm.updatePrBody` — but no SCM provider implements `updatePrBody` (checked `_createGithubProvider`, `_createGitLabProvider`, `_createAdoProvider` in `js/common/scm.js`; the string appears only in this consumer and in test mocks). In production the else-branch below always logs "SCM provider does not support updatePrBody" and returns false — so both this freeze and the new `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping are exercised only by mock-SCM unit tests and change no live behavior.

I also searched the rest of the tree: no JS code path edits an existing PR body (merge bot, smAgent, pushReworkChanges, developTicketAndCreatePR, postMobileTestAutomationResults all only *read* bodies or post comments). That means the `Closes #952` line landed on #956's body at the merge moment from outside the JS automation — most plausibly an agent session in the finalizing run editing the body via `gh` (the rework/dev legs have `bash` in `CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` and produce `outputs/pr_body.md`).

**Ask:** trace the actual write path for dev PRs and put the freeze there — e.g. a pre/post-JS guard that refuses `gh pr edit --body*` while `ai_validating` is on the PR, or a prompt-level rule in the rework/dev instructions. Alternatively, implement `updatePrBody` on the GitHub provider so the machine owns the body rewrite deterministically and this guard becomes live code. As shipped, the ticket AC ("the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms") is not demonstrably satisfied.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

Fixed. Extracted the label scan from `isPrBodyFrozen` into a `mergeQueueBodyLabelPresent(labels)` helper in `js/common/pullRequest.js`, exactly along the suggested lines. `isPrBodyFrozen` is now a flat predicate (CC ≈ 6 → CRAP ≈ 6 at full coverage) and the helper ≈ 5, both under the gate's threshold of 8. Behavior is unchanged — the existing `pullRequest helper > body freeze (gh-960)` tests (merged / closed / merged-state / `ai_validating` as `{name}` object and plain string / unrelated labels / null-PR cases) all pass unmodified, and the full suite is green (3705 passed, 0 failed).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

Fixed — both halves of the ask are now covered:

1. **The seam is live.** `scm.updatePrBody` is now implemented on the GitHub provider in `js/common/scm.js` (`_githubUpdatePrBody`): `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{id} -X PATCH -F body=@<temp-file>`, the same established `gh api` shell-out pattern as `updateBranch()`. The body goes through a temp file (deleted in a `finally`) so no shell quoting can mangle multi-line Markdown; the method returns the gh output or `null` + a warn on failure. The gh-960 freeze in `postReworkBodyAndComment` and the `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` wrapping in `updatePullRequestBody` therefore now execute against the real provider instead of only mock-SCM tests — pinned by 4 new tests in `js/unit-tests/test_scmGithubProvider.js`.

2. **The agent-side dev-PR write path is fenced.** Since no JS code path edits a dev PR body today, the incident-time write could only have come from an agent shell. Added a HARD RULE to `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md` and `instructions/rework/rework_instructions.md`: never edit the PR body (`gh pr edit --body*`, `gh api …/pulls/N -X PATCH -f body=…`) once the PR carries `ai_validating` or is merged/closed — the body is final from the moment validation arms (gh-960, live #956/#952); post a comment instead.
